chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the dowry (mahr), so he said: "It is what people agree upon, or twelve waqiyah, or five hundred dirhams."

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "In place of that, whatever is entitled to a wage from crafts and teaching a chapter of the Quran or a verse from it serves as equivalent. He narrated that."

key_terms.الْمَهْرِ: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: A silver coin used as a standard unit of currency in Islamic law
key_terms.وَقِيَّةً: A unit of weight for gold, typically 60 dirhams

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible forms and amounts for a Muslim dowry (mahr) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the flexibility of the dowry (mahr), establishing mutual consent as the primary principle while providing specific default amounts (twelve waqiyah or five hundred dirhams) in the absence of agreement. Shaykh al-Tusi adds that non-monetary services, such as craftsmanship or teaching Quranic verses, are valid equivalents, reflecting the Shia juristic view that any valuable consideration agreed upon by the parties is permissible. This underscores the pragmatic and consensual nature of marital contracts in Shia fiqh, where the dowry serves as a right of the wife rather than a fixed statutory fee.
